blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.14
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.14

blocks.text: यथा तत्र तथान्यत्र
blocks.directed: [slowly] यथा तत्र तथान्यत्र

blocks.text: Yathā tatra tathānyatra.
blocks.directed: Yathā tatra tathānyatra.

blocks.text: As there, so elsewhere.
blocks.directed: As there, so elsewhere.

blocks.text: Doesn’t Matter Where You Go, Śiva’s Already There.
blocks.directed: Doesn’t Matter Where You Go, Śiva’s Already There.

blocks.text: Now, this is a magnificent little statement.
blocks.directed: Now, this is a magnificent little statement.

blocks.text: Four words.
blocks.directed: Four words.

blocks.text: And Kṣemarāja uses it to explain the universality of the freedom just described.
blocks.directed: And Kṣemarāja uses it to explain the universality of the freedom just described.

blocks.text: Let’s unpack it.
blocks.directed: Let’s unpack it.

blocks.text: Yathā — just as, in whatever manner.
blocks.directed: Yathā — just as, in whatever manner.

blocks.text: Tatra — there.
blocks.directed: Tatra — there.

blocks.text: Tathā — so, likewise.
blocks.directed: Tathā — so, likewise.

blocks.text: Anyatra — elsewhere.
blocks.directed: Anyatra — elsewhere.

blocks.text: As there, so elsewhere.
blocks.directed: As there, so elsewhere.

blocks.text: Now the question is:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Now the question is:

blocks.text: What exactly is being compared?
blocks.directed: What exactly is being compared?

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja answers by referring to the yogi’s manifestation of freedom.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja answers by referring to the yogi’s manifestation of freedom.

blocks.text: Just as the yogi experiences the divine power of manifestation in their own body, so that power is understood to operate elsewhere.
blocks.directed: Just as the yogi experiences the divine power of manifestation in their own body, so that power is understood to operate elsewhere.

blocks.text: The practitioner who is steadily established in recognition doesn’t confine freedom to one particular location.
blocks.directed: The practitioner who is steadily established in recognition doesn’t confine freedom to one particular location.

blocks.text: And the traditional interpretation includes an extraordinary claim.
blocks.directed: And the traditional interpretation includes an extraordinary claim.

blocks.text: The realised yogi is said to be capable of manifesting divine freedom beyond the limits of their own bodily situation.
blocks.directed: The realised yogi is said to be capable of manifesting divine freedom beyond the limits of their own bodily situation.

blocks.text: That is part of the commentary’s metaphysical and yogic claim, rather than merely a poetic statement about feeling peaceful while travelling.
blocks.directed: That is part of the commentary’s metaphysical and yogic claim, rather than merely a poetic statement about feeling peaceful while travelling.

blocks.text: But it also has a deeply illuminating nondual significance.
blocks.directed: But it also has a deeply illuminating nondual significance.

blocks.text: Because if consciousness is the fundamental reality of the manifest universe, then its nature isn’t ultimately restricted to one particular physical location.
blocks.directed: Because if consciousness is the fundamental reality of the manifest universe, then its nature isn’t ultimately restricted to one particular physical location.

blocks.text: Think about the ordinary individual.
blocks.directed: Think about the ordinary individual.

blocks.text: They experience themselves as situated here.
blocks.directed: They experience themselves as situated here.

blocks.text: Within this body.
blocks.directed: Within this body.

blocks.text: At this time.
blocks.directed: At this time.

blocks.text: Surrounded by things located elsewhere.
blocks.directed: Surrounded by things located elsewhere.

blocks.text: And these distinctions are perfectly meaningful within empirical experience.
blocks.directed: And these distinctions are perfectly meaningful within empirical experience.

blocks.text: But the Trika claim is that the universal conscious reality is not ultimately divided by those spatial distinctions.
blocks.directed: But the Trika claim is that the universal conscious reality is not ultimately divided by those spatial distinctions.

blocks.text: The limited standpoint is localised.
blocks.directed: The limited standpoint is localised.

blocks.text: The supreme reality is not.
blocks.directed: The supreme reality is not.

blocks.text: And the realised yogi recognises that distinction.
blocks.directed: And the realised yogi recognises that distinction.

blocks.text: Now consider the practical implication without exaggerating the supernatural claims.
blocks.directed: Now consider the practical implication without exaggerating the supernatural claims.

blocks.text: Suppose someone has a profound meditative experience.
blocks.directed: Suppose someone has a profound meditative experience.

blocks.text: They sit quietly.
blocks.directed: They sit quietly.

blocks.text: Their mind becomes still.
blocks.directed: Their mind becomes still.

blocks.text: There’s an extraordinary sense of openness.
blocks.directed: There’s an extraordinary sense of openness.

blocks.text: The usual sense of separation temporarily relaxes.
blocks.directed: The usual sense of separation temporarily relaxes.

blocks.text: And they conclude:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And they conclude:

blocks.text: “Wonderful. This is where I experience Śiva.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Wonderful. This is where I experience Śiva.”

blocks.text: Then they leave the meditation room.
blocks.directed: Then they leave the meditation room.

blocks.text: Traffic.
blocks.directed: Traffic.

blocks.text: Noise.
blocks.directed: Noise.

blocks.text: People.
blocks.directed: People.

blocks.text: Problems.
blocks.directed: Problems.

blocks.text: And suddenly:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And suddenly:

blocks.text: “Ah, unfortunate. Śiva has apparently remained inside the meditation hall.”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Ah, unfortunate. Śiva has apparently remained inside the meditation hall.”

blocks.text: But if the fundamental nature of consciousness is not confined to that place, why would recognition be restricted to those particular conditions?
blocks.directed: But if the fundamental nature of consciousness is not confined to that place, why would recognition be restricted to those particular conditions?

blocks.text: The same reality is present through the changing circumstances of experience.
blocks.directed: The same reality is present through the changing circumstances of experience.

blocks.text: The task is the stabilisation of recognition, not the construction of an exclusively sacred geographical enclosure.
blocks.directed: The task is the stabilisation of recognition, not the construction of an exclusively sacred geographical enclosure.

blocks.text: And this is precisely where Kṣemarāja connects the sūtra to the yogi’s sustained attention.
blocks.directed: And this is precisely where Kṣemarāja connects the sūtra to the yogi’s sustained attention.

blocks.text: The manifested freedom is described as present wherever the yogi remains established in that recognition.
blocks.directed: The manifested freedom is described as present wherever the yogi remains established in that recognition.

blocks.text: He cites the Svacchandatantra and the Spandakārikā, emphasising the natural, nonartificial character of this freedom. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: He cites the Svacchandatantra and the Spandakārikā, emphasising the natural, nonartificial character of this freedom. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now, compare this with the first book’s teaching that the entire seen world is the body of the realised Self.
blocks.directed: Now, compare this with the first book’s teaching that the entire seen world is the body of the realised Self.

blocks.text: The same metaphysical movement appears again.
blocks.directed: The same metaphysical movement appears again.

blocks.text: The limited individual ordinarily identifies consciousness with a particular organism.
blocks.directed: The limited individual ordinarily identifies consciousness with a particular organism.

blocks.text: But recognition reveals its universal nature.
blocks.directed: But recognition reveals its universal nature.

blocks.text: And therefore the yogi no longer fundamentally confines the Self to the individual body.
blocks.directed: And therefore the yogi no longer fundamentally confines the Self to the individual body.

blocks.text: Now, this doesn’t mean ordinary physical constraints magically disappear for everyone who understands the doctrine.
blocks.directed: Now, this doesn’t mean ordinary physical constraints magically disappear for everyone who understands the doctrine.

blocks.text: You still need to eat.
blocks.directed: You still need to eat.

blocks.text: You still need to sleep.
blocks.directed: You still need to sleep.

blocks.text: You still need to respect other people’s boundaries.
blocks.directed: You still need to respect other people’s boundaries.

blocks.text: And attempting to walk through a wall because you’ve read a Sanskrit aphorism is not an advisable method of testing nondual metaphysics.
blocks.directed: And attempting to walk through a wall because you’ve read a Sanskrit aphorism is not an advisable method of testing nondual metaphysics.

blocks.text: But within the tradition, the deepest freedom of consciousness is not limited by the ordinary spatial identity of the finite subject.
blocks.directed: But within the tradition, the deepest freedom of consciousness is not limited by the ordinary spatial identity of the finite subject.

blocks.text: As there, so elsewhere.
blocks.directed: As there, so elsewhere.

blocks.text: The same Śiva.
blocks.directed: The same Śiva.

blocks.text: The same Śakti.
blocks.directed: The same Śakti.

blocks.text: The same fundamental reality.
blocks.directed: The same fundamental reality.

blocks.text: And now we’ve reached the final sūtra of this instalment.
blocks.directed: And now we’ve reached the final sūtra of this instalment.

blocks.text: And after all this talk about divine freedom, cosmic dancing and the universality of consciousness, Vasugupta has one last instruction.
blocks.directed: And after all this talk about divine freedom, cosmic dancing and the universality of consciousness, Vasugupta has one last instruction.

blocks.text: It’s astonishingly simple.
blocks.directed: It’s astonishingly simple.

blocks.text: But perhaps one of the most practically important in the entire third section.
blocks.directed: But perhaps one of the most practically important in the entire third section.

blocks.text: Pay attention to the seed.
blocks.directed: Pay attention to the seed.
